name: canvas-reveal-effect
title: Canvas Reveal Effect
description: A shader effect that floods its container with a fine grid of dots spreading out from the middle. It appears on hover over a tinted wash and fades away when the pointer leaves.
use: A card or panel should reveal a rich particle texture only when the user points at it.
avoid: It is a WebGL canvas, so it needs a sized parent and a real GPU for smooth dots.
a11y: The reveal is hover-only, so keyboard and touch users never trigger it, and there is no reduced-motion path. (keyboard: no, labels: none, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: Invisible until revealed: then a square fills with a fine grid of tiny glowing dots that gather into a soft cloud near the centre and thin out toward the corners, tinted emerald, pink or blue over a dark wash.
behaves: Pointing at the card makes the dots pop in from the middle outward in a quick burst, with a title fading in over them. Leaving the card fades the whole field back to an empty panel.
customise: Set animationSpeed, dotSize, colours and opacities through props, plus a container background class; the intro shader and gradient fade are fixed in the file.
weight: heavy: A WebGL canvas runs a per-pixel shader at up to 60fps while it is visible.
